chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim from Safwan ibn Yahya, from one who narrated to him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
No one may pray the two rak'ahs of the obligatory Tawaf except behind the Maqam (Station).
And take you the station of Ibrahim as a place of prayer.
If you pray them in any other place, then you must repeat the prayer.

key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: The two rak'ahs of prayer following the obligatory Tawaf

ai.seo_question: Where must the two rak'ahs of Tawaf prayer be performed according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* specifies that the two rak'ahs following the obligatory Tawaf must be prayed behind the Maqam Ibrahim, citing the Quranic command to 'take the Maqam of Ibrahim as a place of prayer.' Shia jurists generally interpret this as a recommended act (mustahabb) rather than a strict condition for validity, though some early scholars held it to be obligatory, necessitating repetition if missed.
